Optional monthly care

Website care

Maintenance, with a content allowance if you want one. The tasks, cadence and monthly fee are agreed in writing.

  • Agreed website maintenance and checks
  • Named backup and recovery responsibilities
  • A defined support route and response targets
  • A record of completed work and open issues
  • Optional, clearly limited content changes
Shape your care brief

Care is optional and separate from the original website project.

Maintain the foundations

Depending on the platform, tasks may include managed updates, checking key pages and links, or testing an agreed enquiry route. We specify which checks are included and how often.

Keep useful information current

Add a content allowance for tasks such as updating opening hours, replacing supplied text or changing an image on an existing page. The agreement defines the limits and how requests are handled.

Know what happened

A care summary records the work completed, any allowance used and issues that still need attention. Its timing and format are agreed with the plan.

Small changes, clearly defined

Keep the details fresh.
Scope the bigger ideas.

Examples help explain the difference. Your written plan confirms which tasks fit your allowance.

Within an agreed allowance

Updates to what’s there

  • Replace supplied text on an existing page
  • Change opening hours or contact details
  • Swap an approved image or document
  • Update an existing service description

Separate scope and approval

Changes to what it does

  • Add new pages or a product showcase
  • Redesign layouts or move platforms
  • Connect a new booking or enquiry tool
  • Reorganise the site’s navigation

No unlimited changes or round-the-clock support. Work beyond the allowance is discussed and approved before it starts.

Fewer loose ends

Know who handles
the important things.

The plan makes ownership and operating responsibilities explicit.

Backups & recovery
Who provides backups, what is covered, frequency, retention and the agreed restore process. Any restore checks are specified, along with who carries them out.
Monitoring & incidents
Whether monitoring is included, what it checks, who receives alerts and how an issue is escalated. Monitoring does not imply round-the-clock human response.
Support & response
The contact channel, working hours and response targets. A response means acknowledgement and assessment; fixing an issue may take longer and depend on other providers.
Costs & renewals
The monthly care fee, any additional-work approval process, and separate hosting, domain, licence or external-tool bills.
Ownership & exit
Who owns the domain, accounts and website files, plus cancellation notice, access handover and any outstanding work at the end of the plan.

Prepare your care brief

A little more clarity

Care should feel
straightforward.

Do I have to choose a care plan?

No. Care is optional. At handover, we explain the website’s maintenance and ownership responsibilities so you can choose how to manage them.

Can you care for a website you didn’t build?

Potentially. We first review the platform, condition, account access and existing responsibilities. Availability and scope depend on that assessment.

How many changes can I request?

Your plan defines the task or time allowance, any limits on requests and whether unused allowance carries forward. We agree how additional work is priced and approved before the plan starts.

Are hosting and website care the same thing?

No. Hosting provides the environment that serves the website. Care covers the work described in your plan. Some providers already handle certain maintenance or backup tasks, so we review that overlap first.

What happens if the website goes down?

Use the agreed support route. We assess the issue within the plan’s working hours and response arrangements, then identify the next step and any provider involvement or extra work. Resolution and recovery depend on the issue and setup.

Can I leave the plan later?

Billing, cancellation notice and handover terms are agreed before care begins. The plan explains access transfer, remaining work and who takes over ongoing responsibilities.
